correctness.rationale: Reconstructed RESULT.md equations (1)–(5). At k=ns_j+m the jth segment has magnitude |sin(mL_j/2)|/(pi |m|) for m nonzero; both signs give 2/pi, and the centers give a bounded contribution. The distinct integer slopes separate the windows, so discarding all other segments within them costs O(1) in total. Outside the windows with |k|=O(n) the same count and denominator bound give O(1). In the remote tail the common 1/k endpoint term cancels by continuity and circle periodicity (the real lift only needs endpoint equality modulo 2pi), leaving O(n/k²), with bounded total. Cesàro averaging and Abel summation give the stated rational and irrational coefficients. The bounded error after replacing the sine sums by a logarithm is claimed only when all lengths are rational. The plateau-tent lengths, both sample evaluations, and continuity at irrationals with a strict downward jump at every rational parameter follow from the denominator formula. The frozen checker was inspected but not run; its finite cutoffs are diagnostic, not the basis for the asymptotic result.

value.rationale: A two-sided logarithmic estimate does not distinguish phases arbitrarily close in the uniform norm. The exact coefficient and its bounded-error harmonic representation explain what length data govern this threshold growth across a natural class, not just an isolated example. The plateau family realizes the effect with fixed slopes and no change in winding, isolating the arithmetic dependence.
